name: Pineapple Mint
summary: Pineapple mint is the variegated cultivar Mentha suaveolens 'Variegata', not peppermint or spearmint. RHS describes its cream-margined foliage, spreading colony, container containment and vegetative propagation.

identity.guidance: Kew recognizes Mentha suaveolens and describes the cultivated Variegata form as pineapple mint. RHS lists the cultivar name and variegated apple-mint aliases. The cultivar is kept distinct from Mentha × piperita and M. spicata.

cultivation.short: A spreading mint with variegated foliage
cultivation.guidance: RHS describes a strong-growing, suckering perennial with cream-margined leaves. It can spread into an extensive colony; restrict the root run or choose a contained growing site. UK garden guidance is retained at its regional scope.

pruning.short: Cut back at the end of the growing season
pruning.guidance: RHS recommends seasonal cutback and notes that division or rhizome planting is an appropriate propagation route. No seed-to-true-cultivar claim is made.

problems.guidance: RHS cautions that the plant can become a nuisance and recommends restricting its root run. This is a garden-spread management issue, not evidence of hydroponic compatibility.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: The reviewed RHS guidance addresses soil and containers, not nutrient-solution performance.

evidence.note: RHS describes the named variegated cultivar as suckering and colony-forming.
RHS reports a maximum height range of 0.1–0.5 m; UK garden context.
RHS reports a maximum spread range of 1–1.5 m; UK garden context.

name: Rau Ram
variety: Species identity; no named cultivar specified
summary: Rau ram is Persicaria odorata, an Asian culinary herb also called Vietnamese coriander. RHS documents seed and vegetative propagation; its outdoor/container guidance does not establish a hydroponic recipe.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Persicaria odorata and lists Polygonum odoratum as a synonym. RHS lists rau ram, Vietnamese coriander and Vietnamese mint among common names. It is not botanical coriander (Coriandrum sativum).

cultivation.guidance: RHS describes a clump-forming plant grown outdoors in summer in rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil and full sun in a sheltered position, with container-under-glass culture for the rest of the year in its UK context. This does not provide controlled-environment nutrient data.

propagation.short: Seed, division, and cuttings are documented
propagation.guidance: RHS lists seed sowing in autumn or spring, division in autumn or spring, and semi-ripe cuttings in summer that root in soil or water. It does not provide a germination-time or temperature value on the reviewed page.

harvest.short: Culinary identity is distinct from cilantro
harvest.guidance: The name Vietnamese coriander is a culinary common name, not a taxonomic synonym for cilantro. Specific harvest frequency and yield are not asserted from the selected sources.

name: Bush Nasturtium
variety: Species-level bush nasturtium type; no cultivar specified
summary: Bush nasturtium is Tropaeolum minus, distinct from trailing T. majus and watercress (Nasturtium officinale). Wisconsin Extension identifies the two garden species separately; its shared sowing guidance is retained at garden-nasturtium scope.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Tropaeolum minus. Wisconsin Extension distinguishes T. minus as bush nasturtium from trailing T. majus. The common name is not confused with watercress, which belongs to a different family and genus.

cultivation.short: Bush type, not the trailing T. majus habit
cultivation.guidance: Wisconsin Extension describes T. minus cultivars among bush nasturtiums, while trailing forms are treated as T. majus. Its general nasturtium advice includes leaner soil and regular moisture during active growth; do not apply trailing-cultivar dimensions to this species.

harvest.short: Flowers are edible in the garden-nasturtium group
harvest.guidance: Wisconsin Extension describes edible flowers for garden nasturtiums. It does not establish a cultivar-specific flavor or harvest schedule for this species identity.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: No source establishes hydroponic compatibility for Tropaeolum minus.

name: Romaine Lettuce
variety: Romaine/cos horticultural type; no cultivar specified
summary: Romaine is a horticultural type within Lactuca sativa, not one named cultivar. This broad identity supports generic romaine references without replacing Red Romaine or named cultivars such as Breen and Pandero.

identity.short: Species identity: Lactuca sativa; romaine/cos type
identity.guidance: Kew accepts Lactuca sativa as cultivated lettuce. Romaine/cos is represented here as a horticultural type; no cultivar is assigned. Red Romaine and named romaine cultivars remain separate identities.

cultivation.short: Use lettuce guidance at crop scope
cultivation.guidance: Lettuce is a cool-season crop and temperature can affect establishment and bolting. Cultivar-specific maturity, head dimensions, heat tolerance, disease resistance, and system spacing are not inferred from this generic type record.

problems.guidance: Temperature response and bolting vary by variety and growing conditions. This species-level profile does not inherit the traits of Red Romaine or any named romaine cultivar.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: No species-level source selected establishes a universal nutrient-solution response for all romaine types.

name: Pinguicula 'Weser'
variety: Registered cultivar name; hybrid of P. moranensis × P. ehlersiae
summary: Pinguicula 'Weser' is a registered cultivated hybrid name, not a botanical species. A research paper reports parentage as P. ehlersiae × P. moranensis; this does not supply a general cultivation or propagation protocol.

identity.guidance: The Pinguicula naming reference explains the cultivar form and ICPS registration role. A 2026 research paper identifies 'Weser' as registered since 1998 and reports P. ehlersiae × P. moranensis parentage. The name is preserved as a cultivar, not converted into a species name.
